How to use this booklet

1Each lesson is four pages. Read the learning intention, copy your teacher's notes into the Notes box, and tick each success criterion when you can do it.
2Pages 1, 2 and 3 are Easy: small steps, one round at a time. Page 4 is Medium, then three worded problems.
WE DOGrey boxes. Your teacher works each example on the board. Copy every step into the space.
YOU DOBlue boxes. Your turn. The ? on each diagram shows what to find. Write the formula, substitute the numbers, then the answer with its unit.
3Some Medium questions come from earlier lessons. The tag (like 11.2 or Year 8) says which one.
4Stuck? Read the Remember line in the blue box, then look back at your notes and the example. Lengths: one decimal place unless the question says otherwise.

In this chapter you will

  • find the length, midpoint and gradient of an interval on the number plane
  • graph straight lines from a table of values, from intercepts and from y = mx + c
  • find the equation of a straight line from its graph or from two points
  • solve linear equations by reading a graph
  • use straight-line graphs and equations to model real situations
  • graph parabolas and use them in real situations

About the artwork

The pictures in this booklet are parts of the Mandelbrot set, drawn by a computer that repeats one simple rule, z → z² + c, thousands of times for every point. Every booklet shows a different part of the set: this one is silver seahorse tails deep in Seahorse Valley, coloured in purple and silver. Maths can make beautiful things.

Acknowledgement of Country

We acknowledge the Bundjalung people, the Traditional Custodians of the land on which Kingscliff High School stands, and pay our respects to Elders past and present.
